ns2:section.sectionText: This course introduces students to experimental instrumentation, acquisition, processing, and storage of CEE-based data at multiple scales of volume, variety, velocity, and veracity; it will also provide a thorough overview and equip students with a working knowledge of modern informatics (e.g., GIS, cloud computing, etc.) as applied to the domain of civil and environmental engineering. Students will analyze and develop sensing and informatics-based solutions to open-ended design problems in primarily cyber-physical system areas of construction management and materials, environmental engineering and science, environmental hydrology and hydraulic engineering, geotechnical engineering, structural engineering, and transportation engineering. The curriculum across all areas of CEE will be enriched as this course will: 1) support any subsequent undergraduate and graduate courses in CEE that may was to include a sensing and/or informatics-based problem solving component and 2) provide new knowledge and skills to CEE students seeking employment and/or pursuing research interests in fields with sensing instrumentation and/or digital spatial data sets (i.e., big data). Some of the course topics are based on recent research findings. The course projects may be able to stimulate new research topics; therefore, this course will be of significance to graduate students and the greater CEE research environment. This course may also be suitable for students from other related disciplines (e.g., computer science, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, biological and agricultural engineering).
